{{short description|American economic statistician}}
'''Selma Evelyn Fine Goldsmith''' (1912–1962) was an American [[economic statistics|economic statistician]] who accurately estimated the personal income distribution of Americans.<ref name="dwe">{{citation|contribution=Selma F. Goldsmith (1912–1962)|pages=80–83|title=Distinguished Women Economists|first1=James|last1=Cicarelli|first2=Julianne|last2=Cicarelli|publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group|year=2003|isbn=9780313303319|contribution-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Liu8A8KjDR0C&pg=PA80}}.</ref>

==Life==
Selma Fine was born in [[New York City]] on January 17, 1912,<ref name=scb>{{citation |title=Selma Fine Goldsmith, Trailblazer in Income Distribution Research|journal=Survey of Current Business|date=June 2021 |url=https://apps.bea.gov/scb/2021/06-june/0621-influencer-goldsmith.htm |access-date=2022-03-11 |publisher=Bureau of Economic Analysis|volume=101|issue=6|first=Mary-Lynne|last=Neil}}</ref> and attended [[Morris High School (Bronx)|Morris High School]] in [[The Bronx]]. She graduated in 1932 from [[Cornell University]] and completed her doctorate in 1936 from [[Harvard University]] with a dissertation on 17th- and 18th-century British business cycles.<ref name="dwe"/>

Fine began working for the [[United States Department of Agriculture]] and then for the National Resources Planning Board, where she began working on income tax data.<ref name=scb/> During this time she married Yale economist [[Raymond W. Goldsmith]].  They had three children. 
Her major publications on income data were produced later, in the 1950s.<ref name="dwe"/>

She died of cancer on April 15, 1962.<ref name="dwe"/><ref name=obit>{{citation |newspaper=The New York Times |date=April 16, 1962 |title=Selma Goldsmith, U.S. Economist, 50; Census Aide, an Authority on National Income, Dies |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1962/04/16/archives/selma-goldsmith-us-economist-50-census-aide-an-authority-on.html |access-date=2022-03-11 }}</ref>

=== Personal life ===
Fine was married to Raymond W. Goldsmith, Professor of Economics at [[Yale University]].<ref name=obit/>

==Recognition==
Goldsmith won the Distinguished Service Award of the [[Department of Commerce]] in 1955, and a Rockefeller public service award in 1956.<ref name="dwe"/>
In 1962, she was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] for "numerous definitive studies clarifying the complex relationships among the statistics relating to the distribution of family income, family expenditures, and the national income accounts".<ref>{{citation|title=New ASA Fellows|page=31|journal=The American Statistician|volume=16|issue=4|date=October 1962|jstor=2681426|doi=10.1080/00031305.1962.10479584}}</ref>

== Published works ==

* 1939.  "The Use of Income Tax Data in the National Resources Committee Estimate of the Distribution of Income by Size," (with Enid Baird), ''Studies in Income and Wealth 3''.
* 1950.  "Statistical Information on the Distribution of Income by Size," ''American Economic Review'' 40.
* 1951.  "Appraisal of Basic Data Available for Constructing Income Size Distributions," ''Studies in Income and Wealth 13''.
* 1953.  "Income Distribution in the United States by Size, 1944–50," (with George Jaszi), Supplement to the ''Survey of Current Business''.
* 1954.  "Size Distribution of Income Since the Mid-Thirties," (with George Jaszi, Hyman Kaitz, and Maurice Liebenberg), ''Review of Economics and Statistics'' 34.
* 1954.  "Inequality of Income Distribution—Discussion," ''American Economic Review'' 44.
* 1956.  "Reply to Dr. Clyman," ''Review of Economics and Statistics'' 38.
* 1957.  "Changes in the Size Distribution of Income," ''American Economic Review'' 47.
* 1958.  "Size Distribution of Personal Income," ''Survey of Current Business'' 38.
* 1958.  "The Relation of [[Census]] Income Distribution Statistics to Other Income Data, An Appraisal of the 1950 Census Income Data," ''Studies in Income and Wealth'' 23.
* 1960.  "Size Distribution of Income and Wealth in the United States," in Arndt, Helmut (ed.), ''Die Konzentration in der Wirtschaft''.
* 1962.  "Low-Income Families and Measures of Income Inequality," ''Review of Social Economy'' 20.<ref name=scb/>
